subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Bone-modifying agents and cancer cachexia

steps.tx: **Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates** bind avidly to exposed bone mineral, which is largely **hydroxyapatite** (a calcium phosphate crystal). During resorption, an **osteoclast** (the cell that breaks down bone) takes up the drug. Inside the cell, the drug blocks **farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP) synthase**, an enzyme in the **mevalonate pathway** (a chain of reactions that makes cholesterol and lipid anchors). This stops **protein prenylation** (attaching lipid anchors to proteins), disrupts protein trafficking, and may push the osteoclast into **apoptosis** (programmed cell death).
steps.say: Nitrogen containing bisphosphonates attach strongly to exposed bone mineral, which is largely a calcium phosphate crystal called hydroxyapatite. During bone resorption, an osteoclast, the cell that breaks bone down, takes the drug up. Inside the cell, the drug blocks farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase, an enzyme in the mevalonate pathway. That block disrupts protein trafficking and may push the osteoclast into apoptosis, which is programmed cell death.

steps.tx: A **skeletal-related event (SRE)** includes bone pain needing opioids, radiotherapy or surgery to bone, **hypercalcemia** (high blood calcium), pathological fracture, and **spinal cord compression**. In randomized trials of men with **castration-resistant prostate cancer**, intravenous **zoledronic acid**, dosed every 3 to 4 weeks, cut SREs by 25%. These drugs lower skeletal events but do not improve overall survival. Guidelines advise starting bone-targeted therapy at diagnosis of bone metastases and continuing it alongside systemic treatment.
steps.say: The term skeletal related event covers much more than broken bones. It includes bone pain that needs opioids, radiotherapy or surgery to bone, high blood calcium, fractures through weakened bone, and pressure on the spinal cord. In randomized trials of men with castration resistant prostate cancer, intravenous zoledronic acid given every 3 to 4 weeks reduced these events by 25 percent. Bone targeted drugs did not change overall survival, so they protect the bone without changing survival. Treatment should begin at diagnosis of bone metastases and continue alongside cancer therapy.

rows: Local treatment of a painful or weakened bone
Excess calcium released from resorbing bone
A break through bone weakened by tumor
Tumor pressing on the spinal cord

steps.tx: Kidney function decides whether an **intravenous aminobisphosphonate** can be given. These drugs are **contraindicated** (must not be given) when **glomerular filtration rate (GFR)** (a measure of how well the kidneys filter blood) falls below 35 milliliters per minute per 1.73 square meters. Above that level, doses still need adjusting to **renal function**. **Zoledronic acid** and **pamidronate** share this class, so the same limit applies to both. For hypercalcemia, **pamidronate** is given as 60 to 90 milligrams over 2 to 4 hours.
steps.say: Kidney function decides whether an intravenous aminobisphosphonate can be given. When the glomerular filtration rate, which measures how well the kidneys filter blood, falls below 35 milliliters per minute per 1.73 square meters, these drugs should not be given. Above that level, doses still need adjusting to kidney function. Zoledronic acid and pamidronate are in this class, so the same limit applies to both. For hypercalcemia, pamidronate is given as 60 to 90 milligrams over 2 to 4 hours.

rows: Doses still adjusted to renal function
Denosumab is the alternative, see next step

steps.tx: **Denosumab** is a fully human **monoclonal antibody** that binds **RANKL**, a signal that drives osteoclast formation and activity. It is not a bisphosphonate. The **reticuloendothelial system** (immune cells that clear material from blood) removes it, so kidney function does not limit it, and it does not adversely affect renal function. The trade-off is calcium: grade 3 or higher **hypocalcemia** (low blood calcium) occurred in 5% on denosumab versus 1% on zoledronic acid.
steps.say: Denosumab takes a different route altogether. It is a monoclonal antibody that blocks RANKL, so it is not a bisphosphonate at all. The reticuloendothelial system clears it rather than the kidneys, and it does not harm kidney function, which makes it the preferred option when renal impairment is significant. The trade-off is calcium. In the phase 3 trial, grade 3 or higher hypocalcemia occurred in 5 percent of denosumab patients, compared with 1 percent on zoledronic acid. Vitamin D deficiency, low calcium intake, and advanced kidney disease raise that risk.

right.title: Zoledronic acid (bisphosphonate)
points: Binds bone mineral and enters osteoclasts

steps.tx: **Cancer cachexia syndrome (CCS)** (a wasting syndrome with loss of appetite, weight loss and muscle loss) may develop in as many as 80% of people with advanced cancer. Clinically important **unintentional weight loss** is more than 5% of body weight over 6 to 12 months. CCS is staged as **pre-cachexia**, **cachexia**, or **refractory cachexia**. The earliest stage is the best time for preventive care, while refractory cachexia carries a life expectancy under 3 months.
steps.say: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome marked by loss of appetite, weight loss, and loss of muscle. It can appear in as many as 80 percent of people with advanced cancer. Doctors look for weight loss of more than 5 percent over 6 to 12 months. The syndrome is staged in three steps. The earliest stage, pre-cachexia, is the best time for preventive measures, while refractory cachexia is the end stage, with a life expectancy of under 3 months.

rows: Weight loss up to 5%, anorexia, glucose intolerance
Weight loss over 5%, or low body mass index (under 20) with over 2% loss, plus inflammation and reduced intake
Cancer resistant to therapy, poor performance status, life expectancy under 3 months

steps.tx: Cachexia is driven by **cytokines** (signaling proteins that promote inflammation), although reduced eating also contributes. **Tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha)** raises fat breakdown and muscle breakdown, though most of that evidence comes from animal models. **Interferon gamma** potentiates fat breakdown and lowers protein synthesis. **Interleukin 1 (IL-1)** induces anorexia and triggers release of **interleukin 6 (IL-6)**, which causes severe wasting and is easy to measure in serum.
steps.say: Cachexia is driven by cytokines, which are signaling proteins that promote inflammation, although reduced eating also plays a role. Tumor necrosis factor alpha raises fat breakdown and muscle breakdown, but most of that evidence comes from animal models. Interferon gamma speeds up fat breakdown and reduces protein synthesis. Interleukin 1 suppresses appetite and triggers the release of interleukin 6. Interleukin 6 causes severe wasting, and unlike tumor necrosis factor, it is easily found in the blood serum of patients.

rows: Fat breakdown, muscle breakdown, higher glucose turnover
Faster fat breakdown, less protein synthesis
Anorexia, early satiety, release of IL-6
Severe wasting, found easily in serum

steps.tx: **Leptin** is a hormone made by fat cells (adipocytes) that reduces appetite and increases **resting energy expenditure (REE)**, the energy the body burns at rest. It acts through signals in the hypothalamus of the brain. In cachectic patients, leptin levels stay persistently low. This pattern suggests that tumors can mimic leptin, keeping appetite suppressed and sustaining weight loss.
steps.say: Leptin is a hormone made by fat cells, and it normally lowers appetite while raising resting energy use. Its effect runs through signals in the hypothalamus of the brain. In cachectic patients, its levels are persistently low. This pattern indicates that tumors can mimic leptin's signal, which sustains anorexia and weight loss. Leptin is therefore a separate piece of the picture from the inflammatory cytokines.

right.title: Leptin
points: Lowers appetite, raises resting energy expenditure

steps.tx: **Anabolic steroids** act through the **androgen receptor (AR)**, a **ligand-activated transcription factor** (a protein that switches genes on or off once a hormone binds it). Testosterone acting on this receptor increases **satellite cells** (muscle progenitor cells) and enlarges muscle fibers. In men with **human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)** and weight loss, testosterone raised lean body mass and muscle strength. **Oxandrolone**, an oral androgen, carries a risk of **hepatotoxicity** (liver injury). In cancer, anabolic steroids have no proven nutrition benefit, and testosterone is contraindicated in men with prostate or breast cancer.
steps.say: Anabolic steroids act through the androgen receptor, a receptor that switches genes on or off once a hormone binds it. Testosterone acting on this receptor increases satellite cells, which are muscle progenitor cells, and enlarges muscle fibers. In men with HIV and weight loss, testosterone raised lean body mass and muscle strength. Oxandrolone, an oral androgen, can injure the liver. In cancer, anabolic steroids show no proven benefit for nutrition status, and testosterone is contraindicated in men with prostate or breast cancer.

Fiber enlargement and more satellite cells
Testosterone raised lean mass and strength
No proven nutrition benefit; testosterone contraindicated in prostate or breast cancer
